items.summary: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

items.title: Physicist Christopher Stubbs joins Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Dr. Christopher Stubbs, an experimental physicist and former Dean of Science at Harvard University, has joined Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust. He brings to the Trust decades of scientific expertise across observational cosmology and precision measurement. items.title: Measuring AI capabilities in intelligence targeting and conventional weapons
items.summary: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team developed new evaluations to measure AI capabilities in tactical intelligence targeting and conventional weapons development.

items.title: Claude computes a nine-loop amplitude in N=4 super-Yang-Mills
items.summary: Claude computes a nine-loop amplitude in N=4 super-Yang-Mills

items.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
items.summary: GLM-5.3 can autonomously build end-to-end cyber exploits, but unlike other frontier models, it was released without meaningful safeguards to limit misuse.

items.title: An opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software
items.summary: We’re launching OSS Scanner, an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing. Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.

items.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
items.summary: The decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.

items.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
items.summary: Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across cheap IoT devices like Android TV boxes, with no datacenter needed.

items.title: Investing in the public benefit
items.summary: We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows.

items.title: Using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code
items.summary: Automated attack surface analysis and reduction can meaningfully improve the security of deployed software in the near term. In this post, we preview data we’ve collected from applying attack surface reduction techniques to large open-source codebases using Claude.

items.title: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
items.summary: We asked an internal research Claude model to design minibinders (small proteins that attach tightly to a target) against scorpion neurotoxins.

items.title: Anthropic update on independent evaluators
items.summary: Anthropic announces updates to embedding independent evaluators

items.title: Detecting and preventing distillation attacks
items.summary: We identified coordinated distillation attacks using ~24,000 fraudulent accounts to extract Claude's capabilities.

items.title: Disrupting an AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
items.summary: A report describing a highly sophisticated AI-led cyberattack and how we disrupted it.

items.title: Strengthening safeguards with US CAISI and UK AISI
items.summary: Government red-teamers tested Constitutional Classifiers on Claude Opus 4 and 4.1, uncovering vulnerabilities that strengthened our safeguards.

items.title: Expanding Project Glasswing

items.title: Partnering with Accenture on embedded evaluation
items.summary: We’re partnering with Accenture on independent evaluation of frontier AI—part of our recent commitment to embed evaluators at Anthropic. Both we and Accenture expect to invest at least $1 billion to build capacity in this area over the next five years.
